items.title: AI Spending Fears Hammer Big Tech Stocks
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Senior Editor for Technology and Strategic Industries Mike Shepard tells Bloomberg This Weekend that disappointing Big Tech earnings are intensifying investor concerns about whether massive AI spending will generate sufficient returns, as Alphabet and Intel come under particular pressure. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Shepard also discusses the record $6.3 billion Binance hack and the possibility that North Korean hackers were responsible. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Binance in Talks for Malaysia License after Five-Year Absence
items.author: Suvashree Ghosh
items.content: <article>Binance said it’s in discussions with Malaysian regulators for a licensed business in the country, as the cryptocurrency exchange seeks a route back into a market where authorities have blocked its website and applications.</article>

items.title: SoftBank-Backed OPay Halts IPO to Respond to Regulatory Inquiry
items.author: Loni Prinsloo and Julia Fioretti
items.content: <article>OPay Ltd., a Nigeria-focused payments platform, halted an initial public offering on the New York Stock Exchange that was supposed to start trading on Friday, citing a regulatory inquiry.</article>

items.title: The Betting Coup That Rocked London’s Bookmakers Goes Unsolved
items.author: Sujata Rao
items.content: <article>Lisa Lazarus, the top cop in US horse racing, woke up one morning this summer to find a flurry of missed overseas calls and e-mails. They were all from UK regulators and they all delivered the same urgent message: a series of large, unusual and suspiciously successful wagers on US races had been placed in London the day before, saddling some of the city’s famed betting parlors with hefty losses, and they needed her help.</article>

items.title: OpenAI’s Altman Meets Samsung Executives as Chip Crunch Deepens
items.author: Yoolim Lee
items.content: <article>OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman met with Samsung Group’s top executives in South Korea on Saturday to deepen cooperation on memory chips and AI infrastructure as global shortages intensify.</article>

items.title: OpenAI Funding Target Cut by $10 Billion as AI Slumps, FT Says
items.author: Yoolim Lee
items.content: <article>OpenAI has cut its fundraising target by $10 billion as an AI stock selloff and rival Anthropic PBC’s impending public listing complicate its efforts to secure investor commitments, the Financial Times reported.</article>

items.title: NYSE Owner Plans Hyperliquid Perpetuals Market in US
items.content: <article>Intercontinental Exchange joined forces with one of the market operators behind offshore crypto-trading platform Hyperliquid as it seeks to bring perpetual futures products into US regulated markets. ICE and Trade.xyz are planning a new market for trading perpetual futures contracts, with its own clearing, know-your-customer and anti-money laundering systems. Jeff Sprecher, Intercontinental Exchange Founder, Chair and CEO, joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss the agreement, plus Friday's major tech selloff,  the growing demand for perpetual futures trading, and more. Sprecher speaks with Tim Stenovec and Jess Menton.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Baseten to Raise Funding That Would Double Value to $30 Billion
items.author: Rebecca Torrence and Bailey Lipschultz
items.content: <article>Artificial intelligence startup Baseten is set to raise new funding that would more than double its valuation to about $30 billion, according to people familiar with the efforts.</article>

items.title: Meta’s Rating Outlook Cut to Negative by S&P on AI Spending
items.author: Davide Barbuscia and Riley Griffin
items.content: <article>S&P Global Ratings took an early step toward potentially downgrading Meta Platforms Inc.’s credit rating within the next two years, amid growing pressure on the tech company’s balance sheet stemming from elevated spending tied to artificial intelligence.</article>

items.title: Need To Rethink How AI Infrastructure Is Powered: FuelCell Energy CEO
items.content: <article>FuelCell Energy President and CEO Jason Few discusses public concerns over higher utility bills, water use and fossil-fuel infrastructure. Discussing a proposed project in Newport Township, Pennsylvania, where FuelCell Energy would supply power but is not the developer, Few said communities should have a say and projects should be judged on their actual effects—not rejected simply because they are data centers. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kristine Aquino on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Opay Shares Fail to Trade After Raising $304 Million in US IPO
items.author: Anthony Hughes
items.content: <article>Shares of Opay Ltd., a Nigeria-focused payments platform, didn’t begin trading in New York as expected after the company raised $304 million in a US initial public offering priced at the bottom of the range.</article>

items.title: Illumina CEO on Q3 Results and Business Outlook
items.content: <article>Jacob Thaysen says Illumina delivered a strong third quarter, beat expectations and raised its fourth-quarter outlook. He said the company has moved from essentially flat performance to mid-single-digit growth over the past 18 months and remains committed to its high-single-digit growth target for 2027, with clinical business serving as the main growth driver. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Power On: How Apple Is Deflecting the Duo’s Cracked Display Problem
items.content: <article>On this episode of the Power On podcast, Chris Welch joins Mark Gurman to unpack reports of cracked displays and why Apple’s limited supply has made getting a replacement so difficult. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Apple Overtakes Nvidia to Become World’s Most Valuable Company
items.author: Jeran Wittenstein and Ryan Vlastelica
items.content: <article>Apple Inc. reclaimed the title of world’s most valuable company on Friday, taking the mantle from Nvidia Corp. as investors seek the perceived safety of the iPhone maker amid concerns about artificial intelligence spending.</article>

items.title: Big Tech Holds $3 Trillion in Spending Commitments for AI Boom
items.author: Brody Ford
items.content: <article>The five largest players in the data center race have committed more than $3 trillion in spending over the coming years, pointing to massive ongoing investment in AI infrastructure.</article>

items.title: AstraZeneca CFO on AI, Earnings, Restructuring Plan
items.content: <article>AstraZeneca Chief Financial Officer Aradhana Sarin says the drug company uses AI in almost every aspect of the work they do. She talks beating on earnings, their drug pipeline and how the company approaches dealmaking. She speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Why Electronic Arts Shut Down BioWare And Cancelled ‘Mass Effect’
items.author: Jason Schreier
items.content: <article>Facing financial pressure, the video-game publisher chose ‘Star Wars’ over ‘Mass Effect’</article>

items.title: Tech Stocks Tumble as AI Fears Collide With Earnings Misses
items.author: Emily Forgash
items.content: <article>Tech stocks plunged on Friday for the second day in a row as fears around AI spending collide with disappointing earnings in big tech’s core businesses.</article>

items.title: Intel Suffers Worst Stock Drop in Decades on Weak Forecast
items.author: Ian King
items.content: <article>Intel Corp. suffered its worst stock rout in more than four decades after the PC industry slump and supply-chain snags hurt its forecast, renewing fears about the chipmaker’s turnaround bid.</article>

items.title: Bridgewater CEO Nir Bar Dea on AI Investing, Markets and Leadership | The David Rubenstein Show
items.content: <article>Bridgewater Associates CEO Nir Bar Dea sits down with David Rubenstein for a wide-ranging conversation about the US economy, rising national debt, the dollar and explains how he sees AI reshaping the future of investing. He also reflects on his unconventional path to Wall Street; from struggling in school and spending six years in the IDF to becoming Bridgewater's oldest intern and eventually its CEO. He's on this week's episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This interview was recorded September 25 in New York.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>
